title: Monocyte–HDL interaction does not establish improved CRP prediction beyond component measures: cross-cycle analysis and a legacy-survey challenge
abstract: We tested whether a centered log-monocyte × log-HDL interaction improves CRP >3 mg/L prediction beyond routine demographic, adiposity, leukocyte and component measures. Models trained in 5,057 NHANES 2007–2008 adults were tested in 4,636 separately sampled 2017–2018 adults. Weighted Brier difference was −0.00001946 (95% fixed-model PSU bootstrap interval −0.00009075 to +0.00004837); improvement was not established. Adding component/adiposity quadratics reversed the point estimate. An unchanged-model challenge in 3,944 NHANES III adults with manual differentials gave unweighted difference +0.00002481 (IID interval −0.00017072 to +0.00021628). That legacy sample is enriched for abnormal hematology and does not support national inference. Prior exposure to modern-cycle outcomes, shared survey infrastructure and measurement differences preclude strong untouched external-validation claims. Code, provenance, negative results and author checks are supplied.
